Cognito Access Token Replay Attack [Spoofing, Information Disclosure, CWE-287] on Cognito, API Gateway, Frontend Application: Attackers could capture JWT tokens through various means (XSS, man-in-the-middle attacks, client-side storage exposure) and replay them until expiration to maintain unauthorized access. An attacker intercepts a valid user's token through compromised network traffic or XSS attack, then uses it to make authenticated API calls to access sensitive organization data.

Credential Stuffing Attack [Spoofing, Information Disclosure, CWE-307] on Cognito User Pool, Frontend Application: Attackers use automated tools to test large sets of stolen username/password combinations against the authentication endpoint, exploiting password reuse across services. An attacker obtains a database of leaked credentials and systematically attempts to authenticate to the application, potentially compromising accounts where users have reused passwords.

Insufficient Authorization Controls [Elevation of Privilege, Information Disclosure, CWE-285] on Lambda Functions, API Gateway, DynamoDB Tables: Missing or insufficient authorization checks in Lambda functions could allow authenticated users to access administrative endpoints or sensitive data they shouldn't have access to. A regular user modifies API requests to access admin-only endpoints, potentially gaining access to delegated administrator account information or sensitive policy data.

Trust Boundary Violation [Information Disclosure, Tampering, CWE-501] on Frontend Application, API Gateway, Lambda Functions, S3 Bucket: Insufficient separation between frontend and backend components could expose sensitive configuration, allow direct access to backend resources, or enable unauthorized API access. An attacker discovers backend API endpoints or configuration details exposed in frontend code, leading to unauthorized access or information disclosure.

Step Functions Execution Manipulation [Tampering, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-918] on Step Functions, Lambda Functions, Resource Policy Scan: Attackers could manipulate Step Functions execution by injecting malicious data or exploiting insufficient input validation in Lambda functions. An attacker modifies input data to a Step Functions workflow, causing it to execute unauthorized operations or access unauthorized resources.
